description:
Sites: four /set handlers exceed clippy::pedantic's too_many_lines threshold (100) by ~3x:
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs:294 handle_message_set — 474 lines
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:79  handle_chat_set    — 373 lines
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:766 handle_space_set   — 363 lines
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/emoji.rs:272 handle_emoji_set   — 355 lines

A senior Rust reviewer's instinct is "split into helpers per /set sub-operation (create / update / destroy, or one fn per patch-op family)". The diff would shrink each ~400-line linear narrative into a 50-line orchestrator that delegates to named sub-functions, each independently testable and reviewable.

HOWEVER — this is the canonical extension-server cookie-cutter pattern inherited from jmap-mail-server, the workspace's anointed canonical template (workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates"). Cross-checking:

  $ wc -l crate-jmap-mail-server/src/*.rs
     2578 crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs
     1195 crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs
      984 crate-jmap-mail-server/src/submission.rs
      607 crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mdn.rs
     1218 crate-jmap-mail-server/src/sieve.rs

Mail-server's handle_email_set inside email.rs (2578 lines) is the canonical 'one big handler per object type' shape. Splitting chat-server's handlers without first splitting mail-server's would be a divergent sibling per the propagation rule, which review will catch (and the workspace AGENTS.md says will be reverted).

The correct framing of this finding: it's a WORKSPACE-CANONICAL-SHAPE question, not a chat-server-local one. The decision is whether the kit's canonical extension-server template should:
  (a) keep big single-fn handlers (current), accepting the function-size lint as documented-policy noise, or
  (b) split each /set into per-op sub-functions in jmap-mail-server first, then propagate the same split across all 8 extension-server siblings (~16-24 sub-functions per crate, ~140-200 across the workspace).

Option (b) is the senior-Rust-shop answer. Option (a) is the working-as-intended answer. The trade is testability + reviewability (b wins) vs. cookie-cutter consistency + already-shipped (a wins until the canonical changes).

Recommendation: do NOT change in chat-server alone. File this as a workspace-architectural decision bead for the canonical-template family (parent should arguably be a workspace epic, not this chat-server review epic), then either (i) accept (a) explicitly as policy and silence the lint workspace-wide with #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)] on the canonical, or (ii) plan a sweep that reshapes mail-server first and propagates. Both outcomes resolve the lint; doing nothing leaves the lint as workspace-wide noise that hides the next legitimate hit.

This finding is filed here (under JMAP-x2gd) for review-pass completeness but should be re-parented to a workspace-architectural epic when picked up. No fix in chat-server in isolation.
title: Workspace canonical-template question: handle_*_set handlers are 350-475 lines each, lint vs. cookie-cutter consistency
